He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]]. ==Early life and career== Da Silva was a standout for Ludwigsgymnasium in Munich and was also a member of the MTSV Schwabing in club play, where he averaged 21.0 points, 8.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 2.0 steals and 1.7 blocks per game in the 2016–17 season. He was selected for the NBBL All-Star Game.{{cite news |title=NBA summer basketball for three former Stanford stars |url=https://paloaltoonline.com/news/2017/06/30/nba-summer-basketball-for-three-former-stanford-stars |accessdate=10 February 2020 |work=Palo Alto Online |date=June 30, 2017}} Da Silva also attended the Internationale Basketball Akademie München (IBAM). He signed with [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] on October 25, 2016 despite not meeting coach [[Jerod Haase]], choosing the Cardinal over offers from [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California]] and several [[Ivy League]] institutions. ==College career== After arriving at Stanford, da Silva injured an ankle in practice and missed a month. He averaged 6.2 points and 4.7 rebounds per game as a freshman.{{cite news |last1=Mims |first1=Steve |title=With familiar names like Reid Travis gone, Stanford men's basketball counting on its sophomores |url=https://www.registerguard.com/sports/20181025/with-familiar-names-like-reid-travis-gone-stanford-mens-basketball-counting-on-its-sophomores |accessdate=February 10, 2020 |work=[[The Register-Guard]] |date=October 25, 2018 |archive-date=October 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024225746/https://www.registerguard.com/sports/20181025/with-familiar-names-like-reid-travis-gone-stanford-mens-basketball-counting-on-its-sophomores |url-status=dead }} As a sophomore, he averaged 9.5 points and 6.0 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Chasen |first1=Scott |title=Tipoff time announced for KU basketball vs. Stanford |url=https://247sports.com/Article/tipoff-time-announced-for-ku-basketball-vs-stanford-135563941/ |access-date=February 10, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=September 15, 2019}} Da Silva scored a career high 27 points and had 15 rebounds and three assists on February 1, 2020, in a 70–60 upset of [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]]. As a result, he was named [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] player of the week on February 3.{{cite news |last1=Abeytia |first1=R.J. |title=Oscar da Silva Wins Pac-12 Player Of The Week |url=https://247sports.com/college/stanford/Article/Oscar-da-Silva-Wins-Pac-12-Player-Of-The-Week-143302595/ |accessdate=February 10, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=February 3, 2020}} On February 8, da Silva suffered a mild concussion and lacerated head that required stitches after a collision with Evan Battey of [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]].{{cite news |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=Stanford's Oscar da Silva lacerates head after colliding with Colorado's Evan Battey |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28661723/stanford-oscar-da-silva-lacerates-head-colliding-colorado-evan-battey |accessdate=9 February 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=8 February 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, da Silva was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]].{{Cite web|url=https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200326010600/https://pac-12.com/article/2020/03/08/2019-20-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 26, 2020|title=Pac-12 announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball annual major awards|date=March 9, 2020|website=pac-12.com|access-date=March 9, 2020}} As a junior, da Silva averaged 15.7 points and 6.4 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Bartlett |first1=Nicholas |title=Understanding A Complicated Pac-12 Basketball Season |url=http://oregonsportsnews.com/understanding-a-complicated-pac-12-basketball-season/ |accessdate=April 3, 2020 |work=Oregon Sports News |date=March 25, 2020}} He averaged 18.8 points and 6.8 rebounds per game as a senior. Da Silva was named to the first-team All-Pac-12 and the conference Scholar-Athlete of the Year.{{cite web |title=Stanford's da Silva named Pac-12 Men's Basketball Scholar-Athlete of the Year |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2021/03/10/stanfords-da-silva-named-pac-12-mens-basketball-scholar-athlete-year |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310180105/https://pac-12.com/article/2021/03/10/stanfords-da-silva-named-pac-12-mens-basketball-scholar-athlete-year |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 10, 2021 |website=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |access-date=June 22, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== On March 24, 2021, da Silva announced he had signed on to play for [[Riesen Ludwigsburg|MHP Riesen Ludwigsburg]] of Germany's [[Basketball Bundesliga]] for the remainder of the 2021 season. Following that, he began training in preparation for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Kader komplett: Oscar da Silva wechselt nach Schwaben |url=https://mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de/news/kader-komplett-oscar-da-silva-wechselt-nach-schwaben/ |accessdate=24 March 2021|website=mhp-riesen-ludwigsburg.de|language=de|date=March 24, 2021}} After going undrafted in the 2021 NBA draft, da Silva joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Oklahoma City Thunder 2021 MGM Resorts NBA Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2021/vegas/team/1610612760/thunder |access-date=April 17, 2022 |website=NBA}} On September 30, he signed with [[Alba Berlin]] until 2024.{{cite news |title=Oscar da Silva joins Alba Berlin on multi-year deal |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/oscar-da-silva-joins-alba-berlin-on-multi-year-deal/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 30, 2021 |date=September 30, 2021 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} He won the German championship and the German cup title in 2022. On July 11, 2022, he signed a three-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]].{{Cite web |title=Oscar Da Silva, un interior versàtil per al Barça |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.cat/ca/basquet/primer-equip/noticies |access-date=2022-07-11 |website=www.fcbarcelona.cat |language=ca}} On June 23, 2024, da Silva parted ways with the Catalan powerhouse. On July 4, 2024, da Silva returned to the [[Basketball Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] for [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] on a three-year deal. In March 2025, da Silva had surgery on his right knee and would remain sidelined for several weeks. He suffered a medial ligament injury in his right knee during the Euroleague game against Paris.{{cite web |title=Bayern’s Oscar da Silva undergoes surgery in his right knee - Eurohoops |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1794519/oscar-da-silva-surgery-right-knee-bayern-euroleague/ |website=www.eurohoops.net |access-date=11 March 2025}} ==National team career== In 2016, da Silva played for [[Germany national under-19 basketball team|Germany]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], an international U18 tournament in [[Mannheim]], Germany. He averaged seven points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.7 blocks per game and won the gold medal.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=German forward commits to Stanford |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/German-forward-Oscar-Da-Silva-commits-to-Stanford-105500167/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=4 February 2020 |date=25 October 2016}} Later in the year, da Silva averaged 9.5 points and six rebounds per game for Germany at the [[2016 FIBA U18 European Championship]] in [[Samsun]], Turkey, leading his team to a fourth-place finish.{{cite web |title=da silva Set For FIBA U19 World Cup |url=https://gostanford.com/news/2017/6/30/mens-basketball-da-silva-set-for-fiba-u19-world-cup.aspx |website=Stanford University Athletics |accessdate=4 February 2020 |date=30 June 2017}} He helped Germany to fifth place at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2017 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in [[Cairo]], averaging 10.3 points and four rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=da silva Shines on World Stage |url=https://gostanford.com/news/2017/7/10/mens-basketball-da-silva-shines-on-world-stage.aspx |website=Stanford University Athletics |accessdate=5 February 2020 |date=10 June 2017}} On August 5, 2023, da Silva premiered for the German national team in a friendly game against Sweden where he | 120 || 96 || 27.9 || .539 || .337 || .743 || 5.9 || 1.7 || .8 || 1.0 || 12.0 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Da Silva has a Brazilian father and German mother. His father was a professional [[boxing|boxer]] before immigrating to Germany in the 1990s and owns a Brazilian restaurant in [[Munich]].{{cite web |last1=FitzGerald |first1=Tom |title=Stanford's Oscar da Silva turns out to be a major find |url=https://www.sfgate.com/collegesports/article/German-mystery-man-turns-out-to-be-a-major-find-12519338.php |website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |accessdate=4 February 2020 |date=23 January 2018}} Da Silva has a younger brother, [[Tristan da Silva|Tristan]], who currently plays basketball for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]].{{cite web |title=Cardinal Capsule: Oscar da Silva |url=https://gostanford.com/news/2018/10/23/mens-basketball-cardinal-capsule-oscar-da-silva.aspx |website=Stanford University Athletics |accessdate=4 February 2020 |date=23 October 2018}} At [[Stanford University]], he was a [[biology]] major and has carried out [[stem cell]] research. He is fluent in five languages: English, French, German, Portuguese, and Spanish. Da Silva's favorite player is [[Kevin Durant]].{{cite web |title=Oscar Da Silva talks Stanford and first season in US |url=https://eurospects.com/?p=12579 |website=Eurospects |accessdate=4 February
